hero.t: I turn real operational problems into software used every day.
hero.b:
I built the ERP for Confecções Botezini, used daily: quotes that took around 20–30 minutes now take 2–5.

React and TypeScript, Supabase/Postgres, 619 automated tests across both stores, and AI built into the development process.

sobre.b:
I study Physics at UFSJ and Systems Analysis and Development at Estácio, and I have been coding for about a year.

I learn by building: real problems in quoting, production, inventory and finance become systems used in operations.

I use AI to speed up investigation and implementation; my job is to break the problem down, give context, test the result and own it.

erp.k: Botezini ERP: product, architecture and AI
erp.b:
Three angles in this chapter: the product (who uses it and the flow), the software design (layers, database and business rules) and AI engineering (how tasks are specified for the agent).

Management system used by Confecções Botezini: quotes, orders, production, inventory, finance.

  • Quotes: 20–30 min → 2–5 min
  • 60+ orders placed through the system
  • Standardized inventory and quotes

React, TypeScript, Supabase, Vercel

in.prob: Quotes made by hand, each one different, and inventory nobody could trust.
dec: Postgres (Supabase) with schema-validated data (Zod)
Data synced and cached with TanStack Query
Installable as an app on phone and desktop (PWA)

items.n: From the integration plan, already in the code: an approved order creates the receivable in finance and enters the factory queue on its own, and production and payment status flow back to the order. Sales never has to ask the factory.

items.html: Pageswhat the user seesHooksstate and filters per screenServicesa single facade for the UIRepositoriesone per domain: finance, inventory, CRMPostgresviews, triggers and functions holding the rules
items.n: Screens never talk to the database. Each layer has one job, and money and inventory rules live in the database, where they cannot be skipped.

Payables and receivables come from a single view. A wrong payment is reversed with a date, never deleted: the history stays auditable. Each expense category is suggested from the supplier history, without AI.

items.t: Technical: average cost in the database
items.n: Every stock entry recalculates the weighted average cost in a trigger, with the row locked (FOR UPDATE) so two simultaneous movements cannot corrupt inventory.
The suggested price comes from real cost: fabric at inventory average cost, overhead, labor from factory daily capacity, taxes and margin.

ic.t: Computational physics: what happens at a crystal surface
ic.b:
Undergraduate research at the UFSJ Electronic Structure Lab (PIIC, 2026–2027), advised by Prof. Horácio Wagner Leite Alves. In progress: Part 1, the one-dimensional model, is done and validated.

Python, NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib, DFTB+

in.numl: independent methods reaching the same result
in.prob: In an infinite crystal electrons spread through the whole material. At the surface the symmetry breaks and states appear that decay into the crystal. The complex band structure describes those states.
dec: First understand and validate the concept in a 1D model, where an exact answer exists
Then take the method to the TiO₂ surface with DFTB+
Finally, the TiO₂/Ni interface, a Schottky barrier
Compare against experimental data from the literature

items.n: Left, the bands for real k. Right, the complex-k loop crossing the gap (grey band): states that decay within about 16 Å, around 5 crystal cells.
